analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains role of Mach number in compressible flow, derives density change relation from momentum and isentropic relations and isentropic speed of sound, and describes subsonic transonic and supersonic regimes.

overview.headline: How Mach number controls air compressibility and density change

keyPoints.point: Mach number is the ratio of aircraft speed to the speed of sound in the gas
keyPoints.quote: The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

keyPoints.point: Below 250 mph at low speed observed density of air remains constant so compressibility is small
keyPoints.quote: If the aircraft passes at a low speed, typically less than 250 mph, it is observed that the density of the air remains constant.

keyPoints.point: In subsonic conditions with Mach less than one square is very small so compressibility can be ignored
keyPoints.quote: For low speed, or subsonic conditions, the Mach number is less than one, M < 1, and the square of the Mach number is very small.

keyPoints.point: In transonic flows density change is nearly equal to velocity change and compressibility cannot be ignored
keyPoints.quote: For transonic flows, the change in density is nearly equal to the change in velocity, and compressibility effects cannot be ignored.

keyTerms.gloss: ratio of aircraft or gas speed to speed of sound that sets compressibility influence
keyTerms.quote: The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

keyTerms.gloss: transmission speed of small isentropic disturbances in the flow
keyTerms.quote: The speed of sound is equal to the speed of transmission of small, isentropic disturbances in the flow.

keyTerms.gloss: effect that alters resulting aerodynamic force when air density changes
keyTerms.quote: This compressibility effect alters the amount of resulting force on the aircraft since the aerodynamic force depends on the air density.

keyTerms.gloss: with constant entropy as disturbances are transmitted without loss
keyTerms.quote: small disturbances in the flow are transmitted to other locations isentropically or with constant entropy.

keyTerms.gloss: sharp disturbances that affect lift and drag downstream of the shock
keyTerms.quote: Sharp disturbances generate shock waves that affect both the lift and drag of the aircraft and the flow conditions downstream of the shock wave.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Lets learners explore temperature dependence of sound speed that underlies Mach scaling and compressibility
Models derivation in page order from momentum through isentropic pressure to Mach density relation
Checks regime distinctions for subsonic transonic and supersonic compressibility behavior
componentPlan.focusQuote: For supersonic and hypersonic flows, the density changes faster than the velocity changes by a factor equal to the square of the Mach number.
